templates.title: Fuuz In-House Trial
templates.description: Deploy the Fuuz AI-driven Industrial Intelligence Platform. Unify manufacturing operations across MES, WMS, CMMS, and Quality with built-in DataOps integration, rapid application development, and an event-native architecture — or build your own custom manufacturing applications.
templates.note: For information on how to setup this template please visit our documentation here: https://support.fuuz.com/portal/en/kb/articles/setting-up-in-house-fuuz before you continue.

env.name: FUUZ_LICENSE_KEY
env.label: License key
env.description: The license key provided by Fuuz. After signing up you will receive this in an email. Ensure you copied the entire license key otherwise it will not properly validate.

env.name: MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME
env.label: Mongo Root Username
env.description: Root username for MongoDB. This is used to log into the database and should be kept secure. The value is defaulted to ease of setup for the trial, it's strongly reccomended to create a custom user.

env.name: MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD
env.label: Mongo Root Password
env.description: Root password for MongoDB. This is used to log into the database and should be kept secure. The value is defaulted to ease of setup for the trial, it's strongly reccomended to create a strong password.

env.name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER
env.label: RabbitMQ Root Username
env.description: Root username for RabbitMQ. This is used to log into the RabbitMQ Admin Dashboard and should be kept secure. The value is defaulted to ease of setup for the trial, it's strongly reccomended to create a custom user.

env.name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS
env.label: RabbitMQ Root Password
env.description: Root password for RabbitMQ. This is used to log into the RabbitMQ Admin Dashboard and should be kept secure. The value is defaulted to ease of setup for the trial, it's strongly reccomended to create a strong password.

env.name: SMTP_PORT
env.label: SMTP Port
env.description: Port number for the SMTP server (default is 587)

env.name: SMTP_HOST
env.label: SMTP Host
env.description: Hostname or IP address of the SMTP server

env.name: SMTP_USER
env.label: SMTP User
env.description: Username for SMTP server authentication

env.name: SMTP_PASSWORD
env.label: SMTP Password
env.description: Password for SMTP server authentication

env.name: SMTP_SECURE
env.label: SMTP Secure
env.description: Whether the connection should use SSL/TLS

env.name: SMTP_FROM_EMAIL_ADDRESS
env.label: SMTP From Address
env.description: The email address that will appear in the 'From' field of outgoing emails

env.name: AWS_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
env.label: S3 Access Key
env.description: By default this uses the localstack container running within the stack. If you change this value after storing files you will lose access to those files.

env.name: AWS_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
env.label: S3 Secret Key
env.description: By default this uses the localstack container running within the stack. If you change this value after storing files you will lose access to those files.

env.name: AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME
env.label: Bucket Name
env.description: By default when using the localstack container this will be fuuz-bucket. This only needs to be changed if you are persisting files in S3.

env.name: AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL
env.label: AWS S3 Endpoint Url
env.description: By default this uses the localstack container running within the stack. If you are using localstack, this url will be in the format 'http://localstack.${MFGX_ENTERPRISE_DOMAIN}'. If you change the MFGX_ENTERPRISE_DOMAIN ensure you update this to match. If you change this value after storing files you will lose access to those files. If you are using S3 set this with your regions url (ex: https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com).

env.name: AWS_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE
env.label: AWS S3 Force Path Style
env.description: If you are using S3 instead of localstack set this to No, otherwise leave the default.

env.name: ENABLE_LOCALSTACK
env.label: Enable Localstack
env.description: When true, a proxy route will be setup to direct traffic to the localstack container. If you are using S3 this should be set to false.

env.name: MFGX_ENTERPRISE_DOMAIN
env.label: Enterprise Domain Name
env.description: The domain name used to access the Fuuz In-House application. By default this will resolve to fuuz.localhost so it can resolve to a local machine. The backend service api will always be defined as `api.<domain>`. If you are creating DNS records for this ensure you include both `api.<domain>` and `<domain>` in your DNS configuration.

env.name: JWT_EXPIRES_IN
env.label: Token Expiration
env.description: Duration before a token needs refreshing. Examples: '15m', '2h', '1d'.

env.name: JWT_MAX_AGE
env.label: Token Max Age
env.description: How long a token can live for before the user needs to re-authenticate. This should always be greater than the Token Expiration.

env.name: ALLOW_NON_SSL
env.label: Allow Non SSL Connections
env.description: By default the stack is not configured to use SSL/TLS. Set this to false if you want the proxy to upgrade any HTTP requests to HTTPS. You will need to provide valid certificates for this to work properly.

env.name: CERT_DIR
env.label: Certificate Directory
env.description: Defines where we should look for certificates for the reverse proxy. These aren't required by default as the proxy will generate self-signed certs if no cert is found. The certs need to be named <domain>.crt and <domain>.key to be detected. Review the nginx-proxy logs on startup to determine whether it loaded your certs or generated self-signed ones.

env.name: ENGINE_OPTIONS_CONCURRENCY
env.label: Data Flow Node Concurrency
env.description: How many nodes in a data flow can execute concurrently. Scale further by adding orchestration-worker replicas — each replica adds this many concurrent node executions.

env.name: ENGINE_LOGGING_EXECUTION_SUCCEEDED
env.label: Log Data Flow Node Success
env.description: When true, the engine will log every successful node execution in data flows. It is recommended to leave this as false unless debugging as the database will grow in size rapidly.

templates.title: SORBA SDE
templates.description: The SORBA Smart Data Engine (SDE) is an industrial data collection/gateway device capable of Advanced Edge Analytics & Machine Learning Edge Processing. SORBA-SDE is equipped with multiple communication driver/protocol applicable to the industrial market. The SORBA-SDE is a sensor/hardware agnostic device that serves as your point & click gateway capable of talking to multiple devices in real-time. The SDE provides easy access to equipment for troubleshooting and remote programming support for PLCs & HMIs utilizing a hassle-free easy, set-up approach to your assets.
